title: Update a price everywhere at once, from one list · {name}
description: Keep prices or products in one list, and show it in slides, documents and a website that follows it. Change it once, and every place that shows it follows.
h1: Change a price once. It changes everywhere it shows.
lede: Keep your prices, products or opening hours in one list, and show it in slides, documents and a website. Change a row, and every place that shows it follows, or stays on the version you chose. {name} draws what uses what, so you see what a change touches before you make it.
cta: Try it with a sample price list
try.ask: Make a collection of our five coffees and their prices per bag, then a price list document and a one-page website that both show it, so that a price changed in the collection changes everywhere.
pane.ask: Show our coffee prices in the price list, the trade fair slides, the newsletter and the shop’s website, from one collection.
pane.title: A project’s creations and how they link, drawn by {name}, live
pane.try: This is the map itself, as {name} draws it. Point at a creation to light what it uses and what uses it, follow the links with the arrow keys, or press one.
pane.asked: In {name}, it opens beside your task.
made.name: The coffee roaster’s project
made.ask: In two sentences, say which prices changed this month.

io.title: What goes in. What shows it.
io.why: Keep it once, in a collection or a section of a document. Then ask for it wherever it should show.
io.ins: Prices, products, people, events: rows you change in one place
Excel or CSV, made into a collection on this device
Opening hours or terms, written once
io.outs: A table, a chart or a figure that follows the collection
A table, a figure or a section, as it is now or at a version
Pages whose tables are filled from it each time they’re read or published
A table as it was when the answer was written, with how many changes came since
Tasks run on a schedule, or each time the collection changes
exact.title: Shown, not copied.
exact.why: Copy a price into five files, and one of them goes stale. {name} keeps one list and shows it where you ask, at the version you choose.
exact.cards: Slides, a document or a website hold a link to the collection, never its rows. Change a row, and each shows it the next time it’s drawn, at once where it’s open.
As it is now, the latest version you published, or one you keep: trade fair slides can stay on last month’s prices, and say when a later version is out.
{links}, at the top of each creation, lists what uses it, and {drawn} draws it as a map. Delete a column, and the message that lets you undo it says what still uses it.
where.title: Where your list lives.
where.why: On your device. What links one creation to another is worked out there, and nothing is sent to show it.
where.cards: Your collections and what shows them are plain files in your browser, encrypted. Nothing we can read reaches us.
Sent to an AI only when you ask
A table or a figure is filled on this device. Only an instruction you add, such as a summary of the rows, sends them to the AI you name.
Online only when you say so
A website shows a new price online once you publish it again. {name} never publishes by itself.
catch.items: {name} is free; the AI behind it may not be. Without a sign-up, only the AI on this computer answers.
What other creations show is a collection, or a section of a document or a whiteboard. Slides and websites show them; nothing shows slides or a website.
A website online shows a change once you publish it again: {name} never puts anything online by itself.
An instruction carried out on the rows, such as a summary, costs what its AI costs each time it runs, and runs by itself only while {name} is open.
A link or a Word file made from a document holds the prices as they were when it was made: only {name} reads a collection.
Your work lives in this browser. Clear its data without a backup and it’s gone.
faq.items: Yes, with no account at {name}. The AI that answers may want one: {free} opens a free one, or use a plan you already pay for, or the AI on this computer, with no account at all.
Is it a copy, or the same list?
The same list. Slides, a document or a website hold a link to the collection, not its rows, so there is one place to change.
Can slides keep last month’s prices?
Yes. Publish a version of the collection, and choose it for the slides in {links}: they stay on it until you move them, and say when a later version is out.
How do I see what a change will touch?
Press {links} at the top of the collection, then {drawn} for the map. On Creations, sorted by {map}, the whole project is drawn.
Does my website follow by itself?
In {name}, at once. Online, once you publish it again: {name} never publishes by itself.
Can I start from my spreadsheet?
Yes. In Creations, Create makes a collection from a CSV file or an Excel workbook’s first sheet, read on this device.
end.title: Start with the roaster’s prices.
end.why: The request opens in {name} and is answered at once, or as soon as you choose an AI. Then link your own.
